safety.destinations: Owned loopback fixtures only; external browser requests denied without resolving or forwarding them.
safety.media: Generated locally from canvas; no downloaded media.
safety.testRuntime: Chrome visible, Edge headless; existing full blocker suite retains its documented loopback Reddit hostname alias.

limitations: Cross-origin frame-initiated top navigation can bypass the hook.
A same-host request followed by an HTTP redirect can bypass the hook.
A real visible link to an unwanted destination is still allowed. Page-world tampering and restricted injection are outside the guarantee.
Legitimate script-only external buttons can be stopped; disable the per-site guard and reload when needed.
Older NavigateEvent sourceElement compatibility was simulated with native navigation; no old browser binary or Firefox was tested.
notes: The old guard reproduced the same-tab redirect before the fix (chrome-before-2.log).

Initial fixture failures included an undelivered native click, duplicate form/button ID, navigation-commit timing and a scrolled iframe hit-test race; final input uses rendered positions and trusted-click evidence.
The cross-origin frame failure was retained and reclassified explicitly as uncovered functionality, not a successful protection assertion.
Rule builders were not rerun because this change leaves all list inputs and packaged rule outputs byte-identical.
